newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-WELSH UNDER PRESSURE IN FRIENDLY WITH FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WELSH UNDER PRESSURE IN FRIENDLY WITH FRANCE.

text.p: Several Welsh players are under pressure to perform well in a friendly rugby union international against France in Cardiff on Wednesday, even with a busy season less than a month old.

As well as injured captain Jonathan Humphreys, the Welsh side announced on Tuesday, is notable for the absence of big names such as Scott Gibbs and Scott Quinnell, recently returned from rugby league but still re-adjusting.

With Wales also set to play Italy, Australia and world champions South Africa in one-off tests before Christmas, the selectors have agreed to the league players' request for more time, giving some members of the existing side a stay of execution.

Coach Kevin Bowring is trying to build a team for the 1999 World Cup, but Welsh morale is far from high after two heavy defeats in Australia in June followed by a scratchy win over the Barbarians last month.
Wales have injury concerns with Humphreys sidelined by a hamstring strain and New Zealand-born Hemi Taylor also a non-starter.
Neath hooker Barry Williams comes in for his first cap and Llanelli centre Nigel Davies takes over the captaincy.
France have lost on their last two visits to Cardiff Arms Park, including their 16-15 Five Nations defeat in March, and lack the injured Thomas Castaignede and Olivier Roumat.

The French, though, are equally keen to demonstrate some form before their two tests against the Springboks in November and December and have already had a chance to experiment at the recent Latin Cup.
French coach Jean-Claude Skrela has decided to stick largely with the same squad which went to Argentina in July.
But Castaignede will be replaced in the centre by gifted Stephane Glas while Roumat hands over to Fabien Pelous, one of the revelations of last year's Five Nations championship.

Skrela said: "It's useful for France to play the Welsh before the Springboks tour even though we would have liked to play on a Saturday instead of between French (league) championship matches," he said.

Wales - Wayne Proctor; Ieuan Evans, Leigh Davies, Nigel Davies (captain), Gareth Thomas; Neil Jenkins, Rob Howley; Steve Williams, Kingsley Jones, Mark Williams, Mike Voyle, Gareth Llewellyn, John Davies, Barry Williams, Christian Loader.

France - Jean-Luc Sadourny, Emile N'Tamack, Richard Dourthe, Stephane Glas, Philippe Saint-Andre, Alain Penaud, Philippe Carbonneau, Abdel Benazzi, Richard Castel, Philippe Benetton, Olivier Merle, Fabien Pelous, Franck Tournaire, Marc de Rougemont, Christian Califano.
Subs (from): Raphael Ibanez, Thomas Lievremont, Christophe Mony, Guy Accoceberry, Yann Delaigue, David Berty.
